fichas.title: Architectural Design Process
fichas.summary: The text outlines the architectural design process, from preparing a building programme and exploring room arrangements and site conditions to developing a preliminary design, refining construction and services, obtaining approval, and tendering. It emphasizes careful preparation and review.
spaces: Individual rooms arranged as scaled rectangles
uses: Explore room relationships, orientation, access, and site conditions
Develop and review a preliminary design
Obtain building approval and tender the works

dimensions.label: Recommended rest period after preliminary design
dimensions.context: Advised interval after completing the preliminary design, allowing distance from the work and defects to become more apparent.
dimensions.ocr_raw: a rest period of 3–14 days is advisable

dimensions.label: Building approval examination duration
dimensions.context: Typical examination period by the building approval authority.

dimensions.label: Architect's workload for a large detached house
dimensions.context: Estimated time for the architect to handle the tasks described in the design and approval process.

dimensions.label: Architect's workload for a larger project
dimensions.context: Estimated time for the architect to handle the tasks described for a larger project, such as a hospital.
dimensions.ocr_raw: 3–12 months (for a larger project such as a hospital)

fichas.title: What Is Design?
fichas.summary: Design is described as the organization and construction of space through architectural elements. A building's spatial theme, typology, topography, and architectural elements interact to shape its form and character; building types may evolve beyond their original functions.
uses: Organize spaces around a spatial theme
Relate a building to its function, location, and topography
Develop architectural form through architectural elements

dimensions.label: Period of architectural theory developments mentioned
dimensions.context: The text refers to developments in architectural theory over the last 20–30 years.
dimensions.ocr_raw: the developments in architectural theory in the last 20–30 years
